subject: evs
prompt_en: Why do we cover food and wash our hands before eating?
prompt_hi: Hum khaana dhak ke kyon rakhte hain, aur khaane se pehle haath kyon dhote hain?
answer: To stop microbes from the air, from flies and from our hands getting onto the food; fewer microbes means the food stays fresh longer and we do not fall sick.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Idli batter rising overnight and milk going bad and smelly both happen because of microbes. So what is the difference?
prompt_hi: Raat bhar mein idli ka ghol phoolna aur doodh ka kharaab hokar badboo dena, dono microbes ki wajah se hote hain. Toh dono mein farak kya hai?
answer: In idli batter, helpful microbes ferment it the way we want: it rises and tastes good. In spoiled milk, unwanted microbes grow and make it smelly and unsafe. Some microbes help us and some harm us.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your tiffin has rice and sabzi. On a hot day it sits in a closed bag until 4 pm. What could happen, and how could you prevent it?
prompt_hi: Tumhare tiffin mein chawal aur sabzi hai. Garmi ke din woh band bag mein shaam 4 baje tak pada rehta hai. Kya ho sakta hai, aur ise kaise roka ja sakta hai?
answer: Microbes could grow in the warmth and spoil the food. Eat it at lunch time, keep the bag in a cool, shady place, use a clean, dry box, and do not eat it if it smells sour.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Gardeners make compost from vegetable peels and leaves. What do microbes have to do with it?
prompt_hi: Maali sabzi ke chhilkon aur patton se compost banate hain. Ismein microbes ka kya kaam hai?
answer: Microbes such as bacteria and fungi, along with earthworms and insects, break the peels and leaves down into compost, a rich soil that feeds plants. Here microbes are helpful.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw what a damp slice of bread kept in a warm place might look like on day 1, day 3 and day 6. Write one line under each drawing.
prompt_hi: Garam jagah rakhi geeli bread slice din 1, din 3 aur din 6 pe kaisi dikhegi, uski drawing banao. Har drawing ke neeche ek line likho.
answer: Day 1: fresh, no spots. Day 3: a few small mould spots. Day 6: many fuzzy green, black or white patches spread over the slice, because the microbes keep growing and multiplying.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Bunty finds a fuzzy spot on a slice of bread. He says, 'I'll just pull off that bit and eat the rest.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Bunty ko bread ki slice pe ek roodaar dhabba milta hai. Woh kehta hai, 'Bas woh hissa tod ke baaki kha leta hoon.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Mould spreads tiny threads deep inside soft bread that we cannot see, so the whole slice, and maybe the rest of the packet, can be spoiled. Throw it away.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your little brother says, 'Germs are all bad. I wish there were no microbes at all!' Explain to him what microbes are, how they spoil food, and why some of them are our friends.
prompt_hi: Tumhara chhota bhai kehta hai, 'Saare germs bure hote hain. Kaash koi microbe hota hi nahi!' Use samjhao ki microbes kya hote hain, khaana kaise kharaab karte hain, aur kuch microbes hamare dost kyon hain.
answer: Microbes are tiny living things everywhere; some grow on warm, moist food and spoil it, but others are helpful: they make curd and idli batter and turn waste into compost.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: name two things that help microbes grow fast on food.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: do cheezein batao jinse khaane pe microbes jaldi badhte hain.
answer: Warmth and moisture; leaving food open and touching it with dirty hands also help.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Match each method to its reason. Methods: drying, salting, fridge. Reasons: (a) slows microbes down with cold, (b) removes the water microbes need, (c) pulls water out and makes the food too salty for microbes.
prompt_hi: Har tareeke ko uski wajah se milao. Tareeke: sukhana, namak lagana, fridge. Wajah: (a) thand se microbes ko dheema karta hai, (b) woh paani hata deta hai jo microbes ko chahiye, (c) paani kheench leta hai aur khaane ko microbes ke liye bahut namkeen bana deta hai.
answer: Drying goes with (b), salting with (c), the fridge with (a).

subject: evs
prompt_en: Ask an adult to cut two slices of cucumber. Sprinkle salt on one and leave the other plain. Predict: what will you see on the salted slice after 20 minutes?
prompt_hi: Kisi bade se kheere ki do slice katwao. Ek pe namak chhidko, doosri saadi rehne do. Guess karo: 20 minute baad namak wali slice pe kya dikhega?
answer: Water droplets come out on the salted slice and it turns soft and limp. Salt pulls water out of food, which is why salty food like achaar is hard for microbes to grow on.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Imagine two bowls of the same boiled milk: one kept in the fridge, one left out on a hot day. Predict which goes sour first, and whether the fridge one will last forever.
prompt_hi: Socho, ek hi ubale hue doodh ki do katoriyaan hain: ek fridge mein, ek garam din mein bahar. Guess karo kaunsi pehle khatti hogi, aur kya fridge wali hamesha theek rahegi?
answer: The one left out goes sour first, often within a day in summer. The fridge one lasts a few days but will also spoil in the end, because cold only slows microbes.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Fresh grapes and raisins (kishmish) are kept in two open bowls for a week. Predict which one spoils first, and why.
prompt_hi: Taaze angoor aur kishmish ko do khuli katoriyon mein ek hafte ke liye rakha. Guess karo kaun pehle kharaab hoga, aur kyon.
answer: The fresh grapes, because they have lots of water; raisins are dried grapes with little water, so microbes cannot grow easily on them.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why is there a layer of oil on top of achaar in the jar?
prompt_hi: Achaar ke martaban mein upar tel ki parat kyon hoti hai?
answer: The oil covers the food and keeps air and moisture away, so microbes, especially mould, cannot easily grow on it; together with the salt it keeps the achaar good for months.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why are papads and vadis dried in hot sun before they are stored?
prompt_hi: Papad aur vadiyaan rakhne se pehle tez dhoop mein kyon sukhaayi jaati hain?
answer: The sun dries the water out of them; without water microbes cannot grow, so the papads and vadis last for months.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare how your grandparents might have kept mangoes for the whole year with how a shop keeps mango juice in packets. What is the same idea behind both?
prompt_hi: Tumhare dada-dadi aam ko saal bhar kaise rakhte the, aur dukaan mango juice ko packet mein kaise rakhti hai, dono ki tulna karo. Dono ke peeche ek jaisa idea kya hai?
answer: Grandparents made achaar with salt and oil or aam papad dried in the sun; the shop's juice is heated and sealed in airtight packets, often with sugar. The same idea: stop microbes by removing water, adding salt or sugar, killing them with heat, or keeping air out.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Nani says, 'Always take achaar out with a dry spoon.' Why does this matter?
prompt_hi: Nani kehti hain, 'Achaar hamesha sukhe chammach se nikaalna.' Ye kyon zaroori hai?
answer: A wet or dirty spoon puts water and microbes into the jar, and the achaar can then grow mould.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your family is going on a two-day train journey from Delhi to Chennai. Which foods would you pack so they do not spoil, and why?
prompt_hi: Tumhari family Delhi se Chennai do din ki train yatra pe ja rahi hai. Kaunsa khaana pack karoge jo kharaab na ho, aur kyon?
answer: Dry or low-water foods like thepla, mathri, laddoo, khakhra, roasted chana, dry fruits, achaar, and fruits with peels like bananas. Avoid curd rice, cut fruit, milk sweets and gravy dishes, which spoil quickly in warmth.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Make a table with three columns, food, method and why it works, for papad, mango achaar, milk and frozen peas.
prompt_hi: 3 column wali table banao: khaana, tareeka aur kyon kaam karta hai. Isme papad, aam ka achaar, doodh aur frozen matar bharo.
answer: Papad: sun-drying, removes water. Mango achaar: salt and oil, salt pulls water out and oil keeps air out. Milk: boiling and then the fridge, heat kills many microbes and cold slows the rest. Frozen peas: freezing, very cold stops microbes from growing.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Riya says, 'This paneer has been in the fridge for two weeks, so it's still fine. Fridge food never goes bad.' What would you tell her?
prompt_hi: Riya kehti hai, 'Ye paneer do hafte se fridge mein hai, toh abhi bhi theek hoga. Fridge ka khaana kabhi kharaab nahi hota.' Tum use kya bologe?
answer: The fridge only slows microbes, so after two weeks paneer can spoil. Check its smell, look and date; if in doubt, throw it out, and never taste it to check.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to a friend how three different methods, drying, salting and keeping in a fridge, all stop food from spoiling.
prompt_hi: Ek dost ko samjhao ki 3 alag tareeke, sukhana, namak lagana aur fridge mein rakhna, kaise khaane ko kharaab hone se rokte hain.
answer: Microbes need water and warmth to grow. Drying removes water; salting pulls water out and makes food too salty; the fridge's cold slows microbes down.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: name one traditional and one modern way of preserving food.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: khaana bachaane ka ek purana aur ek naya tareeka batao.
answer: Traditional: sun-drying, salting, achaar, sugar or murabba. Modern: fridge, freezer, sealed packets or cans, packaged boiled milk.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Sort these into wet and dry waste: banana peel, chips packet, used notebook paper, leftover rice, plastic bottle, used tea leaves.
prompt_hi: Inhe geela aur sukha kachra mein baanto: kele ka chhilka, chips ka packet, purane copy ke panne, bacha hua chawal, plastic ki bottle, use ki hui chai patti.
answer: Wet: banana peel, leftover rice, used tea leaves. Dry: chips packet, notebook paper, plastic bottle.

subject: evs
prompt_en: The school puts vegetable peels, dry leaves and one plastic spoon into a compost pit and covers it with soil. Predict what you will find when you dig it up after two months.
prompt_hi: School ne compost pit mein sabzi ke chhilke, sukhe patte aur ek plastic ka chammach daal ke mitti se dhak diya. Guess karo do mahine baad khodne pe kya milega.
answer: The peels and leaves will have broken down into dark, crumbly compost, helped by microbes and earthworms; the plastic spoon will still be there, unchanged.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Put a small cup under a dripping school tap for ten minutes. Before you start, predict: will it collect just a few drops, a few spoonfuls, or a full cup? Then think: how much in a whole day, and in a whole week?
prompt_hi: School ke tapakte nal ke neeche das minute ke liye ek chhota cup rakho. Shuru karne se pehle guess karo: sirf kuch boondein jama hongi, kuch chammach bhar paani, ya poora cup? Phir socho: poore din mein kitna, aur poore hafte mein kitna?
answer: It depends on how fast the tap drips. At about one drop a second, ten minutes gives roughly 30 mL, a few spoonfuls, which is more than a few drops but less than a cup. Over a day that adds up to about 4 litres, and over a week to around 30 litres, a few buckets, so leaks must be reported and fixed.

subject: evs
prompt_en: On a hot afternoon, predict: will the spot under a big neem tree or the open, sunny corner of the playground feel cooler? Go and stand in each for a minute to check.
prompt_hi: Garam dopahar mein guess karo: bade neem ke ped ke neeche wali jagah thandi lagegi ya playground ka khula dhoop wala kona? Dono jagah ek-ek minute khade hoke check karo.
answer: Under the tree. The tree gives shade, and its leaves give out water vapour, which cools the air around it.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why is it useful to keep wet and dry waste in separate bins?
prompt_hi: Geela aur sukha kachra alag-alag dibbon mein rakhna kyon faydemand hai?
answer: Wet waste can be turned into compost and dry waste like paper and plastic can be recycled. Mixed waste gets dirty and smelly, cannot easily be composted or recycled, and ends up in a dump.

subject: evs
prompt_en: There are cleaning staff in your school. Why should students also help keep the school clean?
prompt_hi: School mein safai karne wale staff hain. Phir bhi bachchon ko school saaf rakhne mein madad kyon karni chahiye?
answer: The school belongs to all of us and we make most of the mess. If everyone avoids littering and tidies up after themselves, the school stays clean and healthy, and the staff's work becomes possible.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare two school canteens: in one, all waste goes into one big drum; in the other, there are green and blue bins and a compost pit. What happens to the waste in each?
prompt_hi: Do school canteen ki tulna karo: ek mein saara kachra ek bade drum mein jaata hai; doosre mein hare aur neele dibbe aur ek compost pit hai. Dono jagah kachre ka kya hota hai?
answer: In the one-drum canteen, mixed waste smells, attracts flies and goes to a dump. In the other, wet waste becomes compost for the school garden and dry waste goes for recycling, so much less is thrown away.

subject: evs
prompt_en: At home, which bin should these go in: potato peels, a broken plastic toy, old newspaper, leftover dal?
prompt_hi: Ghar pe ye kis dibbe mein jaayenge: aloo ke chhilke, toota hua plastic ka khilona, purana akhbaar, bachi hui daal?
answer: Green (wet): potato peels and leftover dal. Blue (dry): the broken plastic toy and the old newspaper.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your school has a big roof and runs short of water every summer. Suggest a plan to use the monsoon rain.
prompt_hi: Tumhare school ki chhat badi hai aur har garmi mein paani kam pad jaata hai. Monsoon ki baarish ka faayda uthane ka plan batao.
answer: Rainwater harvesting: collect roof rain through pipes into a covered tank, or lead it into a recharge pit so it soaks into the ground; use it for plants, cleaning and toilets. Keep tanks covered so mosquitoes cannot breed.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw a map of your school. Mark where you would put green and blue bins, a compost pit, a garden, and any tap that leaks. Explain your choices.
prompt_hi: Apne school ka map banao. Dikhao ki hare aur neele dibbe, compost pit, bageecha, aur koi tapakta nal kahaan hai ya kahaan hona chahiye. Apni pasand ki wajah batao.
answer: Bins near the canteen and classrooms; the compost pit in a corner near the garden, away from classrooms and the drinking water tank; the garden in a sunny spot; leaking taps marked for repair.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Pinky's poster says: 'Put plastic, peels and leaves into the compost pit. It turns everything into soil!' What should she fix?
prompt_hi: Pinky ke poster pe likha hai: 'Plastic, chhilke aur patte sab compost pit mein daalo. Woh sab kuch mitti bana deta hai!' Use kya theek karna chahiye?
answer: Only wet waste such as peels, food scraps and leaves breaks down into compost. Plastic does not rot; it must go into the dry-waste bin for recycling.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to a new student how your school stays clean, green and safe, and what they should do to help.
prompt_hi: Ek naye bachche ko samjhao ki tumhara school saaf, hara-bhara aur surakshit kaise rehta hai, aur use madad ke liye kya karna chahiye.
answer: It is everyone's job; sort waste into green (wet) and blue (dry) bins; wet waste becomes compost; close taps and report leaks; care for the plants; follow safety rules such as no running on stairs.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: which colour bin is for wet waste, and what can happen to that waste?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: geele kachre ke liye kis rang ka dibba hota hai, aur us kachre ka kya ho sakta hai?
answer: The green bin; the wet waste can become compost.

subject: evs
prompt_en: What is a zebra crossing, and why is it painted with white stripes?
prompt_hi: Zebra crossing kya hota hai, aur us pe safed dhaariyaan kyon bani hoti hain?
answer: It is the striped part of the road where people should cross; the bright stripes are easy for drivers to see, so they slow down and stop for people walking across.

subject: evs
prompt_en: With an adult watching, in an empty open ground (never on a road), your friend wears a helmet, rides a cycle at an easy, steady speed and presses the brakes. Predict first: does the cycle stop on the spot, or roll forward a little before it stops? What does this mean for a car on a road? (No cycle? Roll a ball across the floor and try to stop it with a gentle tap of your hand.)
prompt_hi: Kisi bade ki nigraani mein, khaali khule maidaan mein (sadak pe kabhi nahi), tumhara dost helmet pehenke aaram se dheere cycle chalata hai aur brake dabata hai. Pehle guess karo: cycle wahin ruk jaati hai, ya rukne se pehle thoda aage jaati hai? Iska sadak pe chalti car ke liye kya matlab hai? (Cycle nahi hai? Farsh pe ball ludhkao aur haath se halke se rok ke dekho.)
answer: It moves forward some distance before stopping. A faster, heavier vehicle needs even more distance, so a car cannot stop at once if someone steps out suddenly.

subject: evs
prompt_en: On a foggy winter morning, one child wears a dark jacket and another wears a light jacket with shiny reflective strips. Predict: which child will a driver see first?
prompt_hi: Kohre wali sardi ki subah ek bachche ne gehre rang ki jacket pehni hai aur doosre ne halke rang ki jacket jis pe chamakdaar reflective patti hai. Guess karo: driver ko pehle kaun dikhega?
answer: The child in the light jacket with reflective strips; dark clothes are hard to see in fog or darkness, while reflective strips shine in headlights.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Imagine a big school bus parked at the roadside, and a child standing right behind it. Predict: can a car driver coming along the road see the child? Can the child see the car? (You can test it with a big box as the bus and a toy car, looking from the toy car's height.)
prompt_hi: Socho, sadak kinaare ek badi school bus khadi hai aur ek bachcha uske theek peeche khada hai. Guess karo: sadak pe aate car driver ko bachcha dikhega? Kya bachche ko car dikhegi? (Bade dabbe ko bus aur khilona car ko car maan ke, car ki oonchai se dekh ke check kar sakte ho.)
answer: No and no: the bus blocks the view both ways, so stepping out from behind it is very dangerous.

subject: evs
prompt_en: In India, why do we look to the right first before crossing a road?
prompt_hi: India mein sadak paar karne se pehle hum pehle daayein (right) kyon dekhte hain?
answer: Vehicles drive on the left side of the road, so the traffic in the lane nearest to you comes from your right. We look right, then left, then right again because new traffic may have come.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why should you never put your hand or head out of the window of a moving school bus?
prompt_hi: Chalti school bus ki khidki se haath ya sir bahar kyon nahi nikaalna chahiye?
answer: Passing vehicles, poles, trees or walls can hit you, and the bus can move close to them suddenly.
